### Front line

According to the Ukrainian open-source mapping project DeepState, Russian forces newly occupied 8.5 square kilometers (5.0 square kilometers of which were previously contested), while another 9.7 square kilometers became newly contested, notably around the settlements of Hirke (41% contested) and Huliaipilske (6% contested) in the Zaporizhzhia region. 

Geolocated footage compiled by the neutral platform GeoConfirmed showed Ukrainian soldiers from the 3rd Army Corps moving through central Novoselivka, while a Russian soldier was filmed displaying a flag to a drone in Novodmytrivka. 

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its "North" grouping continued tightening an encirclement in the Kharkiv region, alleging ongoing fighting for Mykolaivka, Varvarovka, Reznikovo, Nefedovka, and Lobanovka. The Russian ministry also claimed that forces captured the village of Holubkovo in the Zaporizhzhia region, and asserted that assault units pushed deeper into Dobropillia in Donetsk, allegedly taking a park area, a cultural center, and industrial mine structures. These territorial claims remain unverified by independent sources.

### Strikes and losses

The Economist’s war-fire model detected 60 satellite fire signatures classified as war-related across Ukraine, mostly concentrated in Donetsk (20) and Kyiv (16 in the region, 8 in the city).

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed to have intercepted 370 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over 24 hours across multiple Russian regions and adjacent waters (311 overnight and 59 during the day). Russia also claimed massive strikes using precision weapons and drones against Ukrainian defense industrial targets—specifically targeting enterprises allegedly producing "Flamingo" cruise missiles and long-range drones across Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions—as well as port infrastructure and cargo vessels in the Odesa region. Russia further claimed airstrikes hit a bridge and troop deployment points in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk.

Conversely, neutral geolocated reporting from GeoConfirmed documented significant damage to civilian infrastructure following reported Russian strikes. In Pryluky, an attack damaged the Center of Children and Youth. Other reported Russian missile and drone strikes caused residential fires and civilian casualties, including five killed and 25 injured in one partially destroyed apartment building, two killed and nine injured at another site, one civilian killed in a reported missile attack, and four wounded by a reported Geran drone. GeoConfirmed also recorded a damaged Ukrainian volunteer evacuation vehicle. On the Russian side, GeoConfirmed verified an armored vehicle and a target vehicle attacked by Ukrainian FPV drones, an alleged Ukrainian airstrike on a Russian position in Kostiantynivka, and damaged logistical trucks.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence announced that its defense procurement agency contracted 40,000 tactical headphones for 2026 conforming to NATO military standards. Additionally, the ministry announced receipt of a €1.24 billion tranche from the European Union under the Ukraine Support Loan program, earmarked for Ukrainian-made drones, interceptors, and missiles. The ministry also issued informational guidance to soldiers regarding proper layering of winter uniforms.

The Russian Ministry of Defence highlighted tactical operations and published an official statement marking the Day of the Commander of Naval, Submarine, and Air Ships, quoting Russian Navy Commander-in-Chief Admiral Aleksandr Moiseyev congratulating commanders across Russia's fleets.
